title: The Distributive Property
h1: The distributive property, put to work
_notes: Source of truth for the 0.2.2 practice set. Kinds: "num" (default; same as 0.1, the answer is a number), "expr" (the answer is an expression: a = answer, a_read = how it is said; every line and option is checked at several values of the variables; each wrong option has read = how it is said) and "name" (which property an identity shows: show/say/notes are one block each, ⟨…⟩ in show is highlighted; wrong = the other two properties). Implied multiplication (3x, 2(x + 1), x(x + 5)) and · are allowed. Chips: COMM blue, ASSOC purple, DIST yellow, CALC green, REWRITE white. Also "multi" (select all that apply) and "match" (match pairs): see docs/exercises.md.

exercises.read: Four times the quantity x plus three equals four x plus twelve.
say: The four outside is multiplied by each term inside: four times x, and four times three.
Four times three is twelve. Multiplying across a sum is the distributive property.

wrong.why: Nothing just traded places: the 4 multiplied each term of a sum.
wrong.say: no two terms just trade places

wrong.why: Associative only moves parentheses. Here they disappear because the 4 multiplied each term.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: Five times the quantity x plus two.
say: The five outside multiplies every term inside. Five times x, plus five times two.
Five times x is five x, and five times two is ten.

wrong.why: You multiplied only the x by 5. The 2 needs it too.
You added 5 + 2 instead of multiplying.
You multiplied only the 2 by 5.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: Negative three times the quantity x plus four.
say: Distribute the negative three to both terms, sign included. Negative three times x, plus negative three times four.
Negative three times x is negative three x. Negative three times four is negative twelve, so we subtract twelve.

wrong.why: −3 · 4 is −12, not +12. The negative sign goes along.
wrong.say: lose the sign on the twelve

wrong.why: You multiplied only the x by −3.
You dropped the negative sign completely.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: Seven times the quantity two x minus one.
say: Seven multiplies both terms: seven times two x, minus seven times one.
Seven times two x is fourteen x. Seven times one is seven.

wrong.why: You multiplied only the 2x by 7.
You added 7 + 2 instead of multiplying 7 · 2x.
7 · (−1) is −7. The minus sign stays.
wrong.say: turn the minus into a plus

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to find the value.
say: One hundred two is one hundred plus two.
Eight multiplies both parts: eight times one hundred, plus eight times two.
Eight times one hundred is eight hundred. Eight times two is sixteen.
Eight hundred plus sixteen is eight hundred sixteen.

wrong.why: You multiplied only the 100 by 8.
You multiplied 100 by 2 instead of adding the parts.
wrong.say: multiply the parts instead of adding them
split one hundred two into ten and two

exercises.prompt: Select all the expressions that equal 4(x − 3).
exercises.read: Which of these are equal to four times the quantity x minus three? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: So three of them are equal. Four times x is four x, and four times negative three is negative twelve, in any order.

options.say: Four x minus twelve. Four times x is four x, and four times negative three is negative twelve. Equal.

options.why: Only the x was multiplied by 4; the 3 needs it too.
options.say: Four x minus three. Here only the x was multiplied by four. The three needs it too. Not equal.

options.why: The same two terms in another order.
options.say: Negative twelve plus four x. The same two terms in another order. Equal.
Four x plus twelve. The sign is wrong. Four times negative three is negative twelve. Not equal.
x times four, minus three times four. Each term is multiplied by four, just not calculated yet. Equal.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: Negative the quantity x minus six.
say: A negative sign in front of parentheses means negative one times them.
Distribute the negative one. Negative one times x, plus negative one times negative six.
Negative one times x is negative x. Negative one times negative six is positive six.

wrong.why: (−1) · (−6) is +6. The negative flips both signs.
You ignored the negative sign in front.
You flipped the 6 but not the x.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: Two times the quantity three x plus four y minus five.
exercises.a_read: six x plus eight y minus ten
say: There are three terms inside, so the two multiplies all three of them.
Two times three x is six x. Two times four y is eight y. Two times five is ten, and the minus sign stays.

wrong.why: You multiplied only the first term by 2.
wrong.read: six x plus four y minus five

wrong.why: The 2 must reach the last term too: 2 · 5 = 10.
wrong.read: six x plus eight y minus five

wrong.why: 2 · (−5) is −10. The minus sign stays.
wrong.say: turn the last minus into a plus
wrong.read: six x plus eight y plus ten

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property backwards to find the value.
exercises.read: Seventeen times six, plus seventeen times four.
say: Both products have a seventeen. The distributive property works backwards too: seventeen times the quantity six plus four.
Six plus four is ten.
Seventeen times ten is one hundred seventy.

wrong.why: You dropped the second 17.
You went straight left to right, so the 4 multiplied everything.
You added instead of multiplying.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: Negative four times the quantity negative two x plus three.
say: Negative four multiplies both terms: negative four times negative two x, plus negative four times three.
A negative times a negative is positive, so the first part is eight x. Negative four times three is negative twelve.

wrong.why: (−4) · (−2x) is +8x: negative times negative is positive.
You multiplied only the first term by −4.

exercises.prompt: Match each expression with its expanded form.
exercises.read: Match each expression with its expanded form.
exercises.say_answer: Every expression now has its expanded form. Multiply every term inside, and watch the signs.

pairs.say: Six times x is six x. Six times two is twelve. So six x plus twelve.

pairs.why: The minus sign changes the sign of both terms.
pairs.say: The minus sign in front means times negative one. It changes the sign of both terms: negative x plus five.
Negative three times two x is negative six x. Negative three times negative one is positive three.
x times x is x squared. x times negative four is negative four x.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to find the value.
say: The last nine is nine times one.
Now both parts have a nine, so we can pull it out: nine times the quantity ninety-nine plus one.
Ninety-nine plus one is one hundred.
Nine times one hundred is nine hundred.

wrong.why: You added 99 + 9 first, but multiplication comes before addition.
You left out the + 9 at the end.
Once the last 9 helps make 9 × 100, it is already counted.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: x times the quantity x plus five.
say: The number outside can be a variable too. x multiplies both terms: x times x, plus x times five.
x times x is x squared. x times five is five x, with the number written first.

wrong.why: You multiplied only the first term by x.
x · x is x², not 2x. 2x means x + x.
wrong.say: write x times x as two x

wrong.why: x · x is x², and the 5 must be multiplied by x too.

exercises.prompt: Use the distributive property to expand.
exercises.read: Negative five times the quantity two x minus three y plus one.
exercises.a_read: negative ten x plus fifteen y minus five
say: Negative five multiplies all three terms, and each sign goes along.
Negative five times two x is negative ten x. Negative five times negative three y is positive fifteen y. And negative five times one is negative five.

wrong.why: (−5) · (−3y) is +15y: negative times negative is positive.
wrong.read: negative ten x minus fifteen y minus five

wrong.why: You multiplied only the first term by −5.
wrong.read: negative ten x minus three y plus one

wrong.why: −5 must reach the last term too: (−5) · 1 = −5.
wrong.read: negative ten x plus fifteen y plus one
